title: Introduce slabbed-latency metrics, trace heatmap optimizer, and adaptive alert shutters
author: Marisol Vega
description: Motivation: Long-tail latency spikes and noisy percentile signals have made it hard to distinguish sustained regressions from high-variance workloads. This PR introduces a slabbed-latency metric representation (fixed buckets per sequence-length slab), a trace-level heatmap optimizer that pre-aggregates token-latency contributions into a compact 2D rollup, and an 'adaptive alert shutters' layer that automatically tightens or relaxes alert sensitivity per-route based on recent slab variance. Approach summary: 1) Slabbed metrics: we create slabs keyed by sequence-length ranges (0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024) and emit per-slab histograms for latency, tokens, and cost. This preserves latency shape across different request profiles while keeping cardinality bounded. 2) Heatmap optimizer: traces are sampled at a higher rate for outlier slabs and converted to a compact heatmap tile (time-to-token vs token-index). Tiles are compressed with a small bloom-like sketch so they can be joined with traces in the observability UI. 3) Adaptive alert shutters: a new smoothing controller consumes per-slab variance and SLI history to compute per-route alert thresholds; it reduces alert noise in routes with high natural variance and narrows windows where variance drops. Implementation notes: - Runtime: small changes to token-level timers and an additional tag for sequence_slab on the token emitter. A background aggregator service coalesces slab histograms and writes rollups to the telemetry store every 30s. - Tracing: added a trace enrichment step that emit heatmap tiles as trace attachments, along with a compact metadata payload that includes top-3 contributing tokens and their cumulative cost. - Console: new dashboard panels: Slab latency distribution, Slab variance trend, Heatmap explorer (tile browser), and Per-route shutter status with recommended thresholds. - Alerts: new alert type observability/sabre_shutter that exposes shutter state transitions and reasons. Testing and validation: unit tests for slab bucketing, e2e sim harness that replays production traffic samples to verify rollup accuracy, and load tests to confirm aggregator overhead (<2% CPU on p3d test nodes). Rollout plan: feature gated behind 'obs.slabbed_latency' flag, enabled for 10% of tenants for 48h -> 50% for 72h -> global. Observability: dashboards ship with recommended views and a self-serve 'recompute-slab' button to rebuild rollups for a single tenant. Reasoning about uniqueness: this slabbed approach avoids exploding cardinality from sequence-length tagging while exposing fine-grained tail behavior; the heatmap optimizer trades fidelity for compactness in a predictable way. Migration/compatibility: telemetry consumers that expect flat percentiles must switch to slab-aware aggregators; we include a compatibility shim that synthesizes overall percentiles by weighting slab histograms by observed slab distribution. Related work: follows on from ENG-1740 (token-level cost attribution) but focuses on robust tail detection and alert stability.

Marisol Vega: Added mocked clock for aggregator tests and extended the e2e harness wait timeout. Pushed a fix in the last commit.
Pavel Horvath: Shutter controller looks good but we should emit a 'reason_code' tag for every shutter state transition for postmortems.
Marisol Vega: Added reason_code (tenant_load, variance_rise, manual_override) and documented in the runbook.

release_notes: Introduce slabbed latency metrics and heatmap optimizer. Adds new dashboard panels and adaptive alert shutters to reduce alert noise. Feature gated behind obs.slabbed_latency. See docs/observability/slabbed-latency.md for migration and recompute instructions.
